subject.title: Unhandled Playwright assertion error in CRSession._onMessage crashes Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw address this Playwright CDP assertion class with a narrow browser-owned recovery/classifier after live repro, or should the work wait for a broader browser subprocess isolation design?
rationale: Source and dependency inspection show the fatal path remains plausible, but choosing between targeted suppression, reconnect semantics, and process isolation changes the Gateway crash boundary and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Require live repro, then add browser-owned recovery
options.body: Capture the CRSession CDP message path first, then implement the narrowest handler that logs, tears down the affected Playwright connection, and keeps the Gateway alive.

options.title: Design subprocess isolation first
options.body: Pause code repair until maintainers define a browser worker/process boundary that can crash independently from the Gateway.

options.title: Defer until another production repro
options.body: Leave the issue open but do not spend implementation time until a current-main log or reproduction identifies the exact CDP message shape.

recommendation.title: Require live repro, then add browser-owned recovery
recommendation.body: Capture the CRSession CDP message path first, then implement the narrowest handler that logs, tears down the affected Playwright connection, and keeps the Gateway alive.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to both the browser plugin refactor and the global unhandled-rejection setup in the available history.
